name: Eppeltone Engineers Limited
sector: Electricity meters, smart metering and developing utility services
summary: Eppeltone has genuine meter growth but weak cash realization and unresolved current financing. At ₹136.05 on 19 October 2026, historical P/E is 14.25 x. CAP and R remain NS; BQS, Growth Quality and IAS have no point scores. G2/G3 are holds, not findings of fraud or default. Waaree’s 24.21% secondary stake supplied no issuer capital. Classification: speculative expansion watchlist, not a supported new-investment case.
identity_note: Exact legal identity and security independently matched by ISIN in NSE master and bhavcopy. Eppeltone Energy and Eppeltone Ene. are input aliases only, not duplicate instruments.

quote.kind: official closing trade, not executable bid

score_note: BQS 88% coverage, bounds 4.32-5.40; GQS 85%, raw bounds 5.50-6.85, persistent CASH ceiling 5 but still NS; IAS 40%, bounds 2.00-7.40, nested bounds 2.83-6.25. Missing CAP and R are not replaced with neutral defaults.

gates.reason: No severe abuse established; connected dealings, lender cooperation and presentation weaknesses require scrutiny.
Material bank-return differences, face-versus-note scope and capital/cash-flow classification are not reconciled sufficiently for capital and cash attribution.
Current usable finance, rollover and post-March collections are unverified; the stale-anchor diagnostic is not an assertion of default.
Active ST eligibility and daily prints verified, but ESM1 and indivisible lots materially constrain execution.

GOV.reason: Disclosures permit tracing the ownership transfer and no promoter pledge is reported. Contrary evidence is repeated non-cooperation with the rating agency, material unexplained bank-return differences and weak financial presentation. Related purchases and remuneration are disclosed but arm’s-length economics need testing. No severe abuse is established; G1 is Conditional, not Fail.

MOAT.reason: Utility approvals, testing infrastructure, manufacturing experience and product integration provide qualification advantages. Concentrated tender customers, replicable peer capabilities and the absence of documented retention, pricing power or exclusive technology limit durability. Design patents are not proof of a broad technological monopoly. Five reflects useful but contestable capability.

REV.reason: The three-year core meter revenue CAGR is 43.19%, giving schedule score 9 capped at 8 for limited comparable operating history and Medium confidence. Five-year reported CAGR28.44% mixes securities trading and a pandemic base. FY26 slowed to 8.37%; no acceleration bonus is awarded. Latest growth and weak collections are disclosed separately rather than erasing historical scale.

DUR.reason: Meter replacement and smart-grid deployment offer an accessible multi-year market, supported by existing utility qualifications. Backlog lacks a full roll-forward; gas, water, railway and AMISP approvals or economics remain incomplete. Six credits an established manufacturing route, not the whole national meter program or an unapproved service annuity.

CAP.reason: The explicit FY23-FY26 change-in-capital proxy is 11.18% on a positive ₹103.02 crore denominator; one-year proxy 1.60%. Securities exit, capital advance transfers, immature property/know-how investment and absent cohort returns prevent defensible attribution to new operating capital. CAP stays NS. Current average ROIC13.61%, or a neutral 5, cannot fill the gap.

CASH.reason: Three-year CFO/PAT is -0.697 x reported and -1.183 x after removing borrowing inflows. FY26 receivables rose ₹41.81 crore on ₹10.41 crore revenue growth; disputed MSME balances rose sharply. Some prior-year cash conversion and predominantly recent receivables are contrary evidence, but do not establish realization. Persistent CASH 2 caps GQS at 5 without resolving NS.

BAL.reason: Positive equity ₹90.72 crore and operating interest cover 6.99 x provide support. But March demand/current debt ₹22.52 crore, restricted/earmarked funds, pending claims and cash absorption constrain flexibility. Current usable limits and renewals are ND. A diagnostic shortfall is not proof of present insolvency; G3 remains Hold rather than Fail.

EXEC.reason: Manufacturing expansion and IPO completion demonstrate delivery capability, while actual 8.37% FY26 growth missed the 30-40% outlook and the new plant was still under construction after its indicated mid-2026 timing. Collection deterioration matters more than untested product announcements. Four reflects mixed execution with a material recent miss.

EARN.reason: Operating value added grew 13.71% and EBITDA9.14%, with modest other income. PAT grew 12.93%, yet weighted-average EPS declined from 11.68 to 10.18 after the IPO, and current-share EPS is 9.55. Restatement and development capitalization complicate normalization. Five credits real operating earnings while withholding credit for uncollected profits or immature intellectual property.

R.reason: No current supported base IRR is available because financing and interim balance sheet claims are unverified. Every ordinary funding diagnostic has a deficit and its IRR is null. Hypothetical rescue Base 13.25% uses new shares and fees; self-consistency does not verify financing or permit scoring R.

D.reason: Receivable impairment, delayed commissioning or a supplier squeeze can require dilutive funding. The rescue Bear ends near ₹82.31,39.50% below entry, despite injected capital. Positive equity and a functioning manufacturing franchise are support, but contingent guarantees and uncertain collections weaken the loss floor. No default is asserted.

P.reason: Historical 14.25 x P/E and 10.92 x EV/EBITDA are not obviously extreme, unlike a software multiple for unapproved services. But the conditional 15% return requires 17.47% annual growth, working-capital improvement and ₹39.66 crore equity under the rescue model. Five reflects balanced headline valuation with material execution and financing dependencies, not a margin-of-safety finding.

L.reason: The 60-session continuous 5% exit estimate 4.81 days initially maps to 7. Whole 1,000-share lots, ST/ESM1, lower recent median activity and unknown bid-ask/queue reduce it explicitly to 3. Only 5 of 20 recent sessions support one lot at 5% participation. All 60 sessions printed, so this is not absolute untradeability.

BQS.bound_type: Mathematical missing-evidence completion bounds, not confidence intervals.
BQS.rounding: Exact Decimal weights and contributions; ROUND_HALF_UP two-decimal displays; NS point scores remain null.

GQS.cap_reason: Persistent CASH 2 caps Growth Quality at 5; CAP remains missing.
GQS.bound_type: Mathematical missing-evidence completion bounds, not confidence intervals.
GQS.rounding: Exact Decimal weights and contributions; ROUND_HALF_UP two-decimal displays; NS point scores remain null.

IAS.bound_type: Mathematical missing-evidence completion bounds, not confidence intervals.
IAS.rounding: Exact Decimal weights and contributions; ROUND_HALF_UP two-decimal displays; NS point scores remain null.

derived_tighter_bounds.method: Propagate BQS bounds through Q25%, R remains 1-10, add known D/P/L 1.40.

ranking_eligibility.reason: CAP is NS and G2 independently concerns material quality inputs; IAS also lacks supported R. G3 Hold alone is not a quality-ranking exclusion.

sections.title: Executive Verdict
sections.text:
Eppeltone Engineers Limited is an established electricity-meter manufacturer with plausible smart-meter growth, but a demonstrated shortage of cash realization. It is not an energy generator and is not a separate instrument called Eppeltone Energy. At the official 19 October 2026 close of ₹136.05, the company has an equity value of ₹176.31 crore. Historical earnings make the price look moderate at 14.25 x P/E, but earnings do not currently describe internally funded growth. The research classification is speculative manufacturing-expansion watchlist, not a verified compounder or a supported new-investment case. [S1-S4]

The central contradiction is unusually clear. FY26 revenue rose 8.37% to ₹134.74 crore and PAT rose to ₹12.38 crore, while receivables increased from ₹27.12 crore to ₹68.93 crore. Reported operating cash flow was negative ₹17.84 crore, and that number includes ₹9.94 crore of short-term borrowing inflows. Removing the financing inflow makes operating cash negative ₹27.78 crore before resolving additional capital-advance and deposit classifications. This is not a cosmetic cash-flow ratio issue: growth consumes liquidity and may change how much of future enterprise value belongs to today’s share. [S1, PDF pp 81-94]

There are genuine positives. Meter revenue has scaled substantially, utility qualification and an in-house testing capability are useful, the IPO added equity, and the business remains profitable. There are also tangible adverse observations: customer concentration, a missed growth outlook, unresolved bank-return differences, disputed supplier balances and a plant still described as under construction after its indicated commissioning period. Waaree Smart Meters bought 24.21% from promoters in August, but that secondary trade did not finance the company and is not treated as a strategic rescue commitment. [S2, S9-S14]

BQS, GQS and IAS remain Not Scorable. CAP and R are missing for specific reasons, not assigned neutral scores. G2 and G3 are holds for reliability and financing, not findings of fraud or default. The standalone equity-rescue Base case returns 13.25% over five years versus the 15% hurdle and requires ₹36.47 crore gross new equity on assumed terms. It is a diagnostic, not a recommendation or a current expected return. The most valuable next evidence is collections, reconciled capital movements and usable bank funding, rather than another order announcement.

sections.title: Research Header, Gates and Data Confidence
sections.text:
The research cutoff is 20 October 2026. Information was retrieved on 21 October but filtered to publication by the cutoff. The entry reference is the NSE closing trade on 19 October, not a current executable quote. The five-year nominal INR, pretax equity hurdle is 15%, tested at 12% and 18%; the terminal horizon is 19 October 2031. All financial amounts are in crore unless expressly labelled otherwise. No allocation or transaction is authorized by this report. [S3-S5, S21]

Identity is resolved by the exact ISIN, NSE symbol and eligible security-master row: Eppeltone Engineers Limited, EEPL, INE11 HF01010, NSE SME, 12,959,312 issued shares and a 1,000-share lot. The prospectus identifies CIN U31909 DL2002 PLC117025. Historical private-company names and the submitted Eppeltone Energy alias are not separate businesses. The reviewed financial perimeter is the standalone issuer; no subsidiary, joint venture or associate is included in the FY26 financial perimeter. [S1-S4]

G1 Integrity is Conditional. The audit is unmodified and ownership/connected dealings are disclosed, but financial presentation and lender-information cooperation need improvement. No finding of diversion, fabrication or abusive transfer is made. G2 Reliability is Hold, unresolved: Note 43 records material bank-return differences and the cash-flow statement includes financing within operations. The latter can be reclassified, but neither the remaining capital movement nor the bank-return scope is adequately explained. This affects cash quality and capital-return attribution. [S1, S16]

G3 Funding is Hold, unresolved. The March balance sheet is stale at October entry; sanctioned limits, current draw, drawing power, covenant headroom, rollover and post-March collections are not verified. Positive accounting equity does not establish accessible liquidity. The model’s assumed repayments are diagnostics rather than claims of actual default. G4 Tradability is Conditional, not Untradeable: active ST eligibility and daily prints are verified, but ESM Stage I, whole lots and limited recent participation make execution materially constrained. [S4-S5, S7, S11, S17]

Confidence is high for identity, quote and historical market activity; medium for sales/profit history after explicit restatement qualifications and for business capability; low for current funding, incremental returns and the investment return. Missing FY27 interim results are not fabricated from presentations. G3 Hold alone does not exclude a business from quality comparison; this issuer is currently excluded because CAP is NS and G2 concerns material quality inputs.

The official capital-market calendar excludes 14 September and 2 October from the 60-session window;20 October was also a trading holiday, making 19 October the last market session before cutoff. Every expected session is matched to a valid complete-market archive, rather than treating a missing file as a zero-volume issuer day. [S23]

The independent 60-session sample runs 24 July-19 October, with 60 traded sessions and no missing issuer prints; the latest 20 run 21 September-19 October. Mean/median daily turnover was ₹94.03/20.80 lakh over 60 sessions and ₹26.52/13.21 lakh over 20. Mean/median volume was 66,233/15,000 shares and 18,600/10,000 shares; median trades 14.5 and 9. The 19 October print comprised 13,000 shares in 13 trades. A few large August days inflate the mean, so the continuous reference uses the lower of mean and median. [S3]

For ₹5 lakh, continuous 2%/5%/10% participation exits take 12.02/4.81/2.40 sessions on 60-day activity and 18.93/7.57/3.79 on 20-day activity. Actual orders require 1,000-share lots: three lots cost ₹4.0815 lakh; four ₹5.4420 lakh. At 5% participation, a session needs 20,000 shares to accommodate one lot. Over 60 days 27 sessions qualify, but over 20 only five; total recent capacity is 11 lots. A four-lot forward exit completed in 17 of 20 possible recent start windows, median eight sessions among completed windows, with three right-censored. At 2%, only two lots fit the entire recent window, so no four-lot start completes. These are historical capacity tests, not forecasts or guarantees. [S3-S4]

REG1 identifies ESM Stage I and active ST trade-for-trade status; the master shows next-session limits ₹129.25-142.85. The consolidated framework specifies 100% margin and trade-for-trade treatment at Stage I. October 9,12 and 13 each closed near+5%;12 and 13 were single-price sessions, and 19 October closed near-5%. These are observed limit-like patterns, not proof of an unfillable queue. The current file also flags fewer than 100 unique PANs in 30 days and irregular SME trading; these surveillance definitions are not contradicted by 60 daily prints. Spread, depth and live counterparty availability are ND. [S3-S5, S17]

sections.title: Scorecard and Calculation Audit
sections.text:
The thirteen factors use the framework’s absolute anchors rather than ranks within the SME universe. GOV 4, MOAT 5, REV 8, DUR 6, CAP NS, CASH 2, BAL 4, EXEC 4 and EARN 5 describe the business; R NS, D 3, P 5 and L 3 describe the investment. Each factor has affirmative evidence, contrary evidence, confidence and an evidence-ID trail in the structured factor audit. A missing factor is neither zero nor five and its weight is never redistributed.

BQS weights are GOV 20%, MOAT 20%, REV 12%, DUR 10%, CAP 12%, CASH 10%, BAL 8% and EXEC 8%. The known contribution is 4.20 on 88% coverage. Allowing only the missing CAP to range from 1 to 10 gives mathematical completion bounds 4.32-5.40. The point score remains NS. These are not probabilities or confidence intervals. GQS means Growth Quality Score, not Governance Quality Score. Its weights are REV 40%, DUR 20%, EARN 15%, CAP 15% and CASH 10%. Known contribution 5.35 on 85% coverage gives raw completion bounds 5.50-6.85. Persistent CASH 2 activates the ceiling of 5, but a clipped bound does not create a measured point score.

IAS uses Q equal to final BQS at 25%, R 35%, D 20%, P 10% and L 10%. Known D/P/L contribute 1.40 on 40% coverage. Canonical missing-factor completion bounds are 2.00-7.40. Propagating BQS’s narrower bounds into Q gives 2.83-6.25. IAS remains NS because Q and R are missing and reliability/current funding are unresolved. No G1 or G3 failure cap is applied because neither gate is failed. G4 is not declared untradeable.

REV is based on the available comparable meter business: ₹45.90 crore in FY23 to ₹134.74 crore in FY26, 43.19% CAGR. The mechanical schedule gives 9, capped at 8 for the short comparable record and Medium confidence. Reported five-year growth of 28.44% includes securities turnover and a pandemic base and cannot justify a higher confidence score. No acceleration bonus is used after the FY26 slowdown. CASH’s adverse score rests on a multi-year ratio of sums and collection evidence, not one noisy quarter. CAP stays NS despite a positive-denominator calculation, since measuring a number is not the same as attributing returns to incremental operating investment.

Every weight, contribution and bound is calculated with Decimal arithmetic and displayed using round-half-up to two places. The canonical JSON retains null scores, raw and capped bounds separately, and the script permits exact reproduction. Shared factors intentionally appear in BQS and GQS, but no additional discretionary penalty is silently stacked onto the composite.

sections.title: Business Overview
sections.text:
Eppeltone designs and manufactures static and smart electricity meters, including single-phase and three-phase products, for utilities, public-sector customers and engineering or turnkey counterparties. The economic product is a qualified device plus associated communication and integration capability, not electricity itself. The company’s existing plant is at Greater Noida. The prospectus describes production, assembly, testing and quality processes, and the annual report presents in-house NABL-approved testing and research capability. These are useful entry requirements in a tender-led market, but do not themselves prove excess returns. [S1, business overview; S2, business chapter]

The ordinary manufacturing cycle begins with tender/customer qualification, component procurement, assembly and testing, followed by delivery or contractually agreed acceptance and eventual collection. Accounting revenue recognizes contractual performance and transfer of risks/rewards; it is not evidence that cash has arrived. Inventory, receivables, customer retentions, performance guarantees and warranty obligations therefore matter alongside the order book. FY26 customer advances were only ₹0.0718 crore, so the disclosed balance sheet does not show customers substantially prefunding the inventory and receivable cycle. [S1, PDF pp 84-86,90]

FY26 manufactured-product revenue was ₹134.7008 crore and services revenue ₹0.0426 crore. The business cannot yet be valued as a mature recurring-service platform. At the September AGM, water and gas approvals were described as advanced, AMISP approval as anticipated, railway prototypes as in field trials, and installation capability as being developed. Those descriptions indicate staged options, not established diversified revenue streams. Any service project may also require upfront infrastructure funding and performance-linked collections; it is not automatically asset-light. [S1, PDF p 95; S9, PDF pp 8-9]

The original capacity table provides an observable operational baseline: annual single-phase capacity 2.0 million units and three-phase capacity 0.1 million, with FY25 production of 1,110,684 and 48,588 respectively. Calculated utilization of 55.53% and 48.59% indicates room in nominal existing capacity. The prospectus prints 49.59% for three-phase utilization, inconsistent with its 48,588 units and 100,000 capacity; the arithmetic 48.59% is used here. Actual bottlenecks can still arise from product mix, testing, electronics assembly or customer specifications; nominal units cannot be multiplied by one arbitrary selling price to promise revenue. Management’s ₹300-350 crore existing-facility potential and ₹500-600 crore combined potential are commercial estimates, not audited demonstrated throughput. [S2, capacity table; S10]

Import dependence is material but not total: imported raw materials represented 25.15% of FY26 consumption, and unhedged foreign-currency trade payables were ₹7.6634 crore. Those payables are already within suppliers, not an extra debt claim. Product quality, communication interoperability, warranty performance and component availability can all change real margins or cash timing. [S1, PDF pp 99-100]

sections.title: Moat / Industry Position
sections.text:
The strongest defensible advantage is qualification and execution history rather than proven intellectual-property monopoly. A supplier able to satisfy utility standards, demonstrate reliable testing and deliver certified meters has an advantage over a new entrant without approvals. Eppeltone’s experience, laboratory and communication-module work support that claim. The counterpoint is that large buyers can qualify multiple suppliers and competitively tender quantities. The prospectus reports no long-term purchase arrangements assuring recurring customer orders. Top-ten customers supplied 85.73% of FY25 revenue, versus 94.73% in FY24 and 91.55% in FY23. Dependence on a small set of award and payment decisions reduces bargaining power. [S2, risks and business chapter]

Domestic comparisons prevent small-company capability from being mistaken for uniqueness. HPL’s FY25 metering, systems and services revenue was ₹1,075.61 crore, compared with ₹852.58 crore in FY24. Its wider electrical-products mix means total-company margins or multiples are not a clean match. Genus’s FY25 report describes 18 million meters of annual manufacturing capacity and established accredited testing. Both are historical operating benchmarks, not current valuation comparables. Their capabilities show that testing and smart-meter assembly are not exclusive to Eppeltone. The report deliberately does not fabricate contemporaneous peer enterprise values from mismatched quotes and financial periods. [S18, PDF pp 21-22; S19, PDF pp 13,34]

Itron is a global business-model benchmark rather than a direct Indian multiple peer. Its 2025 filing separates devices, networked solutions and primarily recurring Outcomes services. That distinction is useful: durable software or managed-service economics require a verified installed base, contracted service revenue and renewal/retention evidence. Eppeltone’s proposed AMISP and installation businesses have not yet supplied such economics. An aspiration to recurring revenue is not a recurring-revenue moat. [S20, Item 1]

The two design patents announced at the AGM are evidence of registered designs, not proof of broad utility-patent protection, irreplaceability or a legal exclusion of competitors. Likewise, approvals for water, gas or railway applications can open addressable markets but may bring new quality, warranty and working-capital requirements. No customer retention cohort, price premium, gross-margin advantage at matched mix or verified market-share gain is disclosed sufficiently to quantify economic switching costs. [S9]

MOAT 5 therefore reflects a useful qualified manufacturing position with contestable economics. A higher score would require durable tender win rates, repeat collections, measured failure rates and a return premium that survives competitive pricing and the full capital burden. The route to a stronger moat is better commercial evidence, not a larger national demand estimate.

sections.title: Revenue Growth & Scale
sections.text:
The six-year reported revenue series is FY21 ₹38.5491 crore, FY22 ₹82.6096 crore, FY23 ₹72.6447 crore, FY24 ₹78.4554 crore, FY25 ₹124.3355 crore and FY26 ₹134.7434 crore. The annual changes are retained in the model rather than hidden behind one CAGR. FY22 and FY23 are not clean meter-only comparatives: securities trading inflated reported sales, with FY23 securities revenue of ₹26.7481 crore and core meter revenue of ₹45.8966 crore. The five-year reported CAGR is 28.44%, the three-year reported CAGR22.87%, and the three-year core comparison 43.19%. The choice of denominator materially changes the growth story and is disclosed. [S1-S2, S6-S8]

Physical evidence supports some genuine industrial scaling. Single-phase output increased from 492,945 units in FY23 to 891,285 in FY24 and 1,110,684 in FY25; three-phase output was 12,355,63,109 and 48,588. Nominal single-phase capacity doubled during the period. These facts support a volume contribution to growth, but FY26 unit output and realized-price/mix decomposition are not supplied in the reviewed financial statements. Therefore, the FY26 increase cannot be allocated precisely between units, pricing, smarter products or customer mix. The tiny service contribution is separately visible and does not explain the reported scale. [S2, capacity table; S1, Note 21]

Latest growth is slower than the historical core CAGR. FY26 revenue rose ₹10.4079 crore, or 8.37%, following FY25 growth of 58.48%. Operating value added, defined here as revenue less materials, traded purchases and inventory adjustment, increased from ₹41.3475 crore to ₹47.0155 crore. It is not labelled gross profit because employee and other manufacturing expenses remain below that subtotal. This suggests better mix or procurement economics, but cannot prove pricing power without units and product contribution margins. [S1, PDF p 82]

Backlog must be interpreted with its own denominator and timing. The June 2025 prospectus referred to approximately ₹650 crore, while the November call and September 2026 AGM referred to approximately ₹416 crore. No complete bridge of opening orders, new awards, execution, cancellations, tax scope, scheduled delivery and aging is available. It is unsafe either to add all subsequent announcements on top of the latest total or to equate the total with next-year cash revenue. Customer advances and guarantees indicate that execution can require funding before collection. [S2, S9-S10]

The ₹500 crore FY28 revenue vision would require about 92.6% annual growth from FY26 over two years. It is treated as management ambition, not the Base forecast. Policy demand, award timing, qualification, capacity ramp-up, components and financing must all align. REV 8 recognizes historical operating growth, while EXEC and CASH separately capture delivery and collection shortcomings; the growth score is not a substitute for either.

sections.title: Growth Quality & Reinvestment Runway
sections.text:
The accessible runway is stronger than the evidence of profitable, self-financed capture. Eppeltone already sells to meter customers and has room in disclosed nominal capacity. Smart-meter replacement and added communication functions can support demand. However, orders must convert to accepted delivery and then cash, with warranties, guarantees and inventory funded along the way. The company does not yet provide a mature customer or product cohort showing repeat orders, contribution margin, working-capital recovery and total invested capital. That prevents assigning the national smart-meter opportunity directly to shareholders. [S1-S2]

The model uses a bottom-up capacity sense-check rather than an unsupported market-share forecast. At an explicitly assumed ₹2,000 per standardized meter equivalent, FY26 revenue corresponds to 0.674 million equivalents; the Bull year-five revenue corresponds to about 2.06 million. These are not actual unit estimates: a different mix or price changes them, and some units would require different production lines. They merely test whether a growth path is obviously beyond the nominal 2.1 million-unit original capacity. Commissioning the new plant and qualifying new products cannot be assumed solely because an arithmetic capacity comparison appears plausible. [S2; model assumptions]

Capital demand is the binding economic question. Core operating working capital, receivables plus inventory less trade payables, was ₹79.7753 crore in March 2026,59.20% of annual revenue. The Base assumes this ratio improves through 58%,55%,52%,50% and 48%, even while sales rise 15% annually. That is a favorable collection/stock-efficiency assumption, not an extrapolation of recent deterioration. It also assumes capex of ₹10/8/6/5/5 crore and an operating EBIT margin of 13%. A Bull 25% growth path uses higher margins but still consumes more capital. [S1; model]

The incremental-return calculation is explicit. Normalized operating NOPAT, EBIT excluding other income taxed at 26%, increased ₹11.5148 crore from FY23 to FY26. Financing invested capital, equity plus debt minus reported cash, increased ₹103.0192 crore. The 11.18% proxy is below much of an analyst 12-17% nominal capital-cost range; the one-year proxy is only 1.60%. Yet those numbers mix securities exit, capital advances, a large IPO, property expenditure and unfinished know-how. Without reconciliation and maturation, they do not isolate the returns earned by a new rupee of operating investment. CAP is NS, not 11.18% translated mechanically into a score. [S1-S2, S6, S8]

GQS therefore remains NS, with a persistent cash-quality ceiling of 5. A high growth rate cannot compensate for unresolved investment economics. Improving the conclusion requires funded commissioning, collection evidence and incremental returns after all capital, not an announced addressable market or a current ROCE snapshot.

sections.title: Management, Governance & Execution
sections.text:
Rohit and Deven Chowdhary remain central operating leaders. The September shareholding filing resolves an important ownership change: the promoter group held 4,869,400 shares,37.57%, while Waaree Smart Meters Private Limited held 3,137,000 shares,24.21%. Regulation 29 disclosures show an off-market purchase on 7 August 2026 from Rohit and Deven, respectively 2,316,000 and 821,000 shares. The total issued count remained 12,959,312. This was not a preferential issue, did not bring cash into Eppeltone, and does not by itself establish a financing guarantee, supply contract or management-control agreement. [S12-S14]

The September XBRL reports no promoter encumbrance and no outstanding convertible securities, warrants or employee options. It also reports 2,595,965 promoter shares locked, about 20.03% of total shares, reducing practical free float beyond the headline public percentage. A December 2025 proposed issue of 15 lakh warrants and 3 lakh equity shares was withdrawn on 31 January 2026. The analysis therefore adds neither hypothetical proceeds nor those shares to the current capital structure. A future raise remains possible, but must be modeled as a new event rather than assumed already available. [S12, S15]

Connected dealings need commercial scrutiny without insinuation. FY26 remuneration to the two directors totaled ₹1.92 crore, about 15.5% of PAT; remuneration payable at year-end was ₹1.0104 crore. Purchases from Amit Export were ₹5.0965 crore and the closing advance ₹0.7866 crore. Promoter loans and family-property advances are disclosed in the related-party note. Their disclosure is a positive, but public documents do not supply matched third-party pricing or a complete economic rationale. No abusive transfer is established by the amounts alone. [S1, PDF p 101]

The statutory audit is unmodified and internal financial controls are reported on. Those are meaningful assurances, not a waiver of analytical reconciliation. Crisil’s April 2026 rating action retained B/Stable and A4 with the Issuer Not Cooperating suffix; limited information, rather than an asserted payment default, is the relevant concern. Note 43’s persistent bank-return differences and the cash-flow financing classification deserve direct explanation even with an unmodified opinion. [S1, S16]

Execution is mixed. The IPO and historical unit expansion happened. Against this, the November 2025 call maintained a 30-40% FY26 growth outlook, while audited growth was 8.37%. The new facility was expected around mid 2026 but was still discussed as construction at the September AGM. New approvals and design patents are milestones, not cash returns. GOV 4 and EXEC 4 reflect observable shortcomings without crossing the framework’s severe-abuse threshold. Evidence of collections, commissioning and disciplined funding would matter more than simply restating the long-term vision.

The IPO raised ₹43.9552 crore gross. TheMarch utilization statement shows ₹30 crore working-capital use, ₹2.32 crore of ₹5 crore machinery allocation spent, and ₹4.3638 crore GCP marked used. It also reports ₹5.5274 crore issue expenses against ₹4.5914 crore estimated, with ₹0.9360 crore excess taken from GCP and ₹0.1575 crore further estimated payment pending. Its total therefore cannot be used without reconciling the GCP reallocation. Net equity cash flow ₹38.3375 crore corresponds to ₹5.6177 crore deducted from gross proceeds, which also requires reconciliation to expense/payment timing. The analysis uses the explicit remaining earmark and escrow conservatively, not the misleading assumption that all headline proceeds remain available. [S1, S11]

sections.title: Financial Forensics
sections.text:
The reproducible historical schedule includes six years of revenue, operating EBIT/EBITDA, PAT, tax-normalized earnings, reported CFO, capex, debt, cash, equity, receivables, inventory, payables, invested capital and bonus-adjusted per-share diagnostics. FY21-22 scans use thousands of rupees and are converted by dividing by 10,000; later financial statements use lakhs and are divided by 100. FY23 original statutory PAT ₹0.3495 crore differs materially from prospectus restated PAT approximately ₹1.086 crore, primarily because of deferred-tax and employee-benefit adjustments. FY24 statutory PAT ₹9.1072 crore and restated ₹8.1586 crore also differ. FY25 restated ₹11.2320 crore is not silently substituted for latest statutory ₹10.9590 crore. The prospectus reconciliation itself contains a missing leading digit in FY25 and a small FY23 inconsistency. Both versions remain visible. [S1-S2, S6-S8]

FY26 revenue ₹134.7434 crore, operating EBIT ₹17.7755 crore, EBITDA ₹19.4101 crore and PAT ₹12.3758 crore are reconciled from the P&L. Operating EBIT equals PBT plus finance cost less other income. Other income was ₹0.7980 crore, finance cost ₹2.5439 crore and depreciation ₹1.6346 crore. Normalizing tax to 26% after excluding other income gives PAT ₹11.2714 crore. This is an analyst normalization, not adjusted management earnings. Technical know-how under development ₹4.5628 crore requires recognition, cost and useful-life support; treating all of it as immediate expense is a stress sensitivity, not an asserted accounting correction. [S1, PDF pp 82,91]

Cash is materially worse than profits. FY24-26 reported CFO totals negative ₹22.6145 crore against PAT ₹32.4420 crore, a ratio of sums of-0.697 x. Removing short-term borrowing inflows of ₹1.8507/3.9647/9.9401 crore makes the ratio-1.183 x. FY26 reported CFO/CFI/CFF of-₹17.8441/-₹19.3228/+₹36.8658 crore reconcile to a ₹0.3011 crore cash reduction. Moving ₹9.9401 crore from operations to financing preserves that total. A further ₹9.7826 crore reduction in capital advances may represent transfer into fixed assets; without proof, the corresponding CFO/capex reclassification is shown only as a sensitivity. It changes categories, not total cash. [S1, PDF p 83; S6]

The balance-sheet transmission is stark. Receivables rose ₹41.8092 crore and inventory ₹11.9908 crore; supplier balances rose only ₹0.9066 crore. Ending DSO is 186.73 days and average-balance DSO130.10 days. Receivables older than six months were ₹6.5906 crore, versus ₹6.2117 crore; the percentage falls because newer balances grew, not because old balances were substantially collected. No doubtful-debt provision is identified in the aging. Disputed MSME payables were ₹10.6422 crore, up from ₹1.8620 crore, a potential collection/supplier-pressure interaction rather than proof of nonpayment. [S1, PDF pp 89,92-93]

Note 43 reports March debtor balances of ₹75.2983 crore to banks versus ₹67.8983 crore in the note’s books, a ₹7.40 crore difference. The face balance sheet is ₹68.9331 crore, leaving another ₹1.0348 crore scope difference. Inventory and creditor differences recur across quarters. The note does not provide a sufficient cause-and-resolution bridge. This is the basis for G2 Hold, not an allegation that either number is fabricated. [S1, PDF p 103]

March debt was ₹39.0076 crore, including ₹22.5238 crore current borrowing, against cash ₹3.3563 crore. Long-term deposits ₹6.5791 crore and security against loans ₹0.8484 crore are not treated as unrestricted net cash; disclosed guarantee margin deposits are encumbered. Guarantees ₹28.8598 crore are contingent, not ordinary debt, and unhedged FX payables ₹7.6634 crore are already inside trade creditors. Capital commitments ₹1.4229 crore enter modeled capex once. Income-tax payable ₹2.9993 crore and statutory liabilities ₹0.9081 crore enter the opening funding bridge once. Warranty provisions total ₹1.3613 crore, based on an estimated 0.5% of covered sales over about five years. [S1, PDF pp 88-100]

The IPO increased shares from 9,525,312 to 12,959,312. Reported weighted-average diluted EPS fell from ₹11.68 to ₹10.18 despite PAT growth; FY26 earnings on the current count are ₹9.55. A historical 1:1 bonus is adjusted in comparisons and is not economic dilution. No current options or warrants are added. Debt/EBITDA after reported cash is 1.84 x and operating interest cover 6.99 x, but those stock ratios do not resolve the cash conversion or rollover problem. [S1-S2, S12]

sections.title: Valuation & Market Expectations
sections.text:
At ₹136.05 and 1.2959312 crore shares, market capitalization is ₹176.3114 crore. Adding March debt and subtracting reported cash gives EV ₹211.9627 crore,10.92 x FY26 operating EBITDA. P/E is 14.25 x reported PAT and 15.64 x normalized PAT; price/book is 1.94 x. This cross-check is transparent but stale-balance-sheet dependent. Long-term restricted deposits are not netted, BGs are not treated as fully called debt, and IPO proceeds are not added again to March cash. These multiples alone cannot show whether growth creates per-share value. [S1, S3-S4]

The explicit return model starts with March operating balances because no newer complete balance sheet is verified. Its annual intervals end on the October entry anniversaries, not invented fiscal half-years. Bear revenue growth is-15%,0%,5%,5%,5%, with 8-10% EBIT margins and core working capital 70% declining to 65% of sales. Base grows 15% annually at 13% EBIT margin, with working capital 58% declining to 48%. Bull grows 25% annually at 15% margin, with 58% declining to 50%. Depreciation is 1.5% of sales, tax 26%, interest 12% of opening debt, and terminal EV/EBITDA8 x/10 x/12 x. All are analyst assumptions, not company guidance.

Capex totals ₹19/34/43 crore in Bear/Base/Bull. Existing current debt is paid in year one and long-term debt evenly over five years as a no-assumed-refinancing stress convention, not a verified contractual schedule. Opening tax/statutory claims are settled once. The ₹2.68 crore IPO machinery earmark is released once against capex, while ₹0.1575 crore issue-expense escrow is excluded from available cash and not charged again. This leaves ₹0.5188 crore starting general cash. The prospectus issue, withdrawn warrants and Waaree secondary purchase are not new funds. [S1, S11-S15]

All ordinary cases show cash-buffer deficits: Bear ₹31.15 crore, Base ₹34.65 crore and Bull ₹51.06 crore. Ordinary IRRs are null, even though unsupported terminal algebra can be calculated. These figures do not prove actual funding failure because interim collections and bank renewals are unknown. They show why an investment return cannot be scored merely by assuming the missing money arrives. Full short-term renewal is separately modeled as an assumption, not verified headroom.

The isolated rescue variant issues equity at ₹108.84,20% below entry, incurs 5% issuance costs and restores a ₹1 crore cash buffer. Gross new equity is ₹32.79/36.47/53.75 crore, producing five-year returns of-9.56%/13.25%/27.63%. Rescue terminal prices are ₹82.31/253.45/460.66; their 15% discounted values are ₹40.92/126.01/229.03. This is an illustrative dilution mechanism, not a financing proposal. Terminal P/E implied by each scenario provides the earnings cross-check, with debt subtracted only once.

The reverse rescue model requires 17.47% annual revenue growth to earn 15%, reaching ₹301.42 crore revenue and requiring ₹39.66 crore gross equity under Base margins and capital assumptions. At 12%/18% hurdles, required growth is 13.27%/21.76%. A two-way grid varies 10/15/20% growth against 8/10/12 x exit EV/EBITDA. Because current financing is not verified, neither the reverse model nor the 13.25% rescue Base is a scoreable R. A price concession alone does not cure missing reliability or liquidity evidence.

There are no intermediate distributions, so terminal value represents 100% of modeled shareholder proceeds; retained cash is already in terminal equity and is not also paid as dividends. A per-side 1%/3%/5% execution-cost sensitivity is supplied, because actual spread and impact cannot be verified. This is not a claim that SME execution will cost those amounts. Rental costs remain operating expenses under the reported accounting basis; no hypothetical IFRS16 lease liability is introduced into an otherwise non-lease-adjusted EBITDA multiple. Unverified additional lease commitments remain a limitation rather than an invented zero. The model also exposes annual net investment, capex less depreciation plus change in ONWC, and its incremental-NOPAT proxy; forecast proxies do not backfill historical CAP.

sections.title: Bear Case & Permanent-Loss Path
sections.text:
The most credible permanent-loss route is not simply lower revenue. It is delayed customer collection combined with inventory that cannot be converted promptly, supplier pressure, and repayment or drawing-power constraints while fixed investment continues. The FY26 receivable increase and disputed MSME balance make this mechanism company-specific. A customer can accept fewer deliveries or defer payment without the manufacturer immediately reporting an operating loss; the cash need can precede the earnings warning. [S1]

Under the Bear diagnostic, revenue falls 15% initially, margins compress, working capital remains high and capex continues at a restrained level. The unfinanced path has a ₹31.15 crore maximum cash-buffer deficit and therefore no valid ordinary equity IRR. Even after an assumed ₹32.79 crore rescue, the terminal price is ₹82.31,39.50% below entry, with a-9.56% annualized return. That outcome is not a forecast of bankruptcy; it illustrates dilution and weaker operating value occurring together. A capital injection can keep a business operating while existing shareholders still lose money.

Receivable quality is a major sensitivity. A10% impairment of March receivables would be ₹6.89 crore before tax, and a 20% inventory haircut ₹11.71 crore. These are analytical stresses, not asserted loss estimates, and should not be added again as cash uses if the same loss already drives working-capital recovery in a scenario. The ₹4.56 crore unfinished know-how balance could also fail to earn its carrying value. Conversely, collectible utility receivables and useful plant retain value, so an automatic zero-recovery assumption would be equally unsupported. [S1, Notes 13-17]

The ₹28.86 crore performance/financial guarantees matter because project failures can produce cash claims; the annual report assesses invocation as remote. The ordinary model therefore does not deduct every guarantee as funded debt. A separately specified 10% invocation stress would be ₹2.89 crore before recoveries, not the entire guarantee amount. Currency exposure can affect procurement economics, but the ₹7.66 crore unhedged payable is already in creditors. A currency loss must not duplicate the principal claim. [S1, Notes 30-32]

Liquidity amplifies practical downside. ST trade-for-trade settlement, ESM surveillance, daily price limits, small lots of counterparties and an unknown order-book queue can make a paper exit price inaccessible. Daily prints do not prove the ability to sell a four-lot position without impact. The thesis breaks if collection and financing evidence fail to improve while growth commitments expand. A persistent unexplained bank-return gap, material write-offs, supplier stoppage or unfinanced capex would warrant reassessment even if the reported P/E falls. D 3 reflects this impairment path, while stopping short of an unsupported default allegation.

sections.title: 5× / 10× Feasibility
sections.text:
A multibagger outcome must be defined by horizon, earnings, capital and ownership rather than a large demand forecast. Fivefold price appreciation requires 37.97% annually over five years,25.85% over seven and 17.46% over ten. Tenfold requires 58.49%,38.95% and 25.89% respectively. These are price returns before dividends and taxes. The report does not assume a cash dividend while the business is funding expansion and working capital.

At the current ₹176.31 crore equity value,5× and 10× imply ₹881.56 crore and ₹1,763.11 crore of equity value before dilution. With a 20 x terminal P/E and 10% PAT margin, those outcomes require approximately ₹44.08/88.16 crore PAT and ₹440.78/881.56 crore sales. Over five years, sales would need to grow about 26.75%/45.60% annually from the FY26 base. At a 15 x P/E, required sales rise to ₹587.70/1,175.41 crore. Lower or more cyclical margins raise those requirements further. Exact seven- and ten-year variants are stored in the model rather than implied by a five-year slogan.

The ownership assumption is crucial. Those simple equations hold shares fixed. The Base rescue increases the share count by about 25.9%, so a given enterprise or total equity value is spread across more shares. A target price needs proportionately more profit if new equity funds expansion. Debt-funded growth avoids immediate share issuance but adds interest, repayment and covenant risk. Neither funding route is free. The current zero outstanding warrants figure prevents phantom present dilution, but does not guarantee that future growth can avoid dilution. [S12; model]

Capital feasibility is also demanding. At 50% core working capital, ₹440.78 crore revenue needs ₹220.39 crore core working capital, compared with ₹79.78 crore today, before the additional plant and technology investment. The 10× sales condition would need about ₹440.78 crore core working capital. Collections could improve and supplier terms could help, but the latest evidence runs in the opposite direction. It is inappropriate to extrapolate revenue at a fixed multiple without making this capital requirement visible. [S1]

Management’s ₹500 crore FY28 vision is near one necessary revenue condition for a 5× outcome at generous but not impossible assumptions; it is not sufficient. It must arrive with sustainable margins, realized cash, financing on acceptable terms and retained ownership. New facilities, smart-meter mix, water/gas approvals, rail qualification and services offer possible routes, but their unit economics are not established. The appropriate conclusion is conditional feasibility, not base-case 5× or 10× potential. No probability-weighted multibagger claim is assigned from the available evidence.

sections.title: Monitoring Plan
sections.text:
1. Collections and aging: baseline March receivables ₹68.9331 crore, ending DSO186.73 days and balances older than six months ₹6.5906 crore. Seek cash collections matched to opening invoices, not only a lower percentage of old balances. A next annual ending DSO above 180 days or rising old-balance rupees without explanation is a warning; sustained movement toward 120 days with independently reconciled receipts would be constructive. Thresholds are analyst monitoring rules, not covenants. [S1]

2. Operating cash: baseline FY26 financing-adjusted CFO-₹27.7842 crore. Require a statement that excludes borrowing proceeds and reconciles capital advances and deposits. Two consecutive comparable reporting periods of positive operating cash and a rolling CFO/PAT ratio approaching 0.8 would support reconsidering CASH; a one-period release without invoice evidence would not settle the issue.

3. Bank returns and funding: reconcile every material Note 43 difference, especially the ₹7.40 crore March debtor gap and the additional ₹1.0348 crore face-versus-note scope gap. Obtain current sanctions, draw, eligible borrowing base, unused capacity, maturities and covenant compliance. Unexplained differences persisting into the next audited period or inability to fund committed capex would keep G2/G3 on hold. A revised rating alone is not a substitute for the liquidity bridge. [S1]

4. Supplier and warranty stress: baseline disputed MSME balances ₹10.6422 crore and warranty provision ₹1.3613 crore. Track settlements, dispute reasons, critical-supplier continuity, failure/return rates and provisions against the five-year warranty exposure. A sharp increase in disputes or product failures without matching provisions is a thesis warning. [S1]

5. Plant and development capital: verify commissioning, installed equipment, commercial acceptance and utilization, not only construction progress. Separate existing plant returns from new facility and ₹4.5628 crore know-how development. Obtain total project cost, remaining spend and returns after working capital. Further timing slippage beyond the next formal project update, or capitalization without identified commercial use, prevents a CAP upgrade. [S1, S9-S10]

6. Backlog quality: baseline management figure ₹416 crore. Require opening-to-closing movement, delivery schedule, cancellations, guarantees, advances and debtor terms. Do not add announced orders twice. Track repeat orders and customer concentration against FY25 top-ten 85.73%. A larger order book with deteriorating collections is not a positive cash signal. [S2, S9-S10]

7. New products and services: require final approvals, first commercial invoices, gross contribution, service duration and collection terms for water/gas, rail, AMISP and installation. Baseline services revenue is ₹0.0426 crore. Only evidenced recurring revenue and funded infrastructure merit service-platform valuation credit. [S1, S9]

8. Ownership and dilution: monitor promoter 37.57%, Waaree 24.21%, pledge, lock-ins, board rights and any new issuer financing. Verify issue price, fees and purpose before changing the share count. A secondary shareholder transaction never enters issuer cash. [S12-S15]

9. Liquidity: refresh eligible series, ESM status, lot size,60/20-session median turnover and whole-lot participation. Baseline recent 5% capacity is 11 lots across 20 sessions, concentrated in five days. Deterioration, suspension or a persistent inability to exit within a suitable horizon can independently prevent an investment action. [S3-S5, S17]

sections.title: Final Classification & Conditional Action
sections.text:
The business is a speculative manufacturing-expansion watchlist candidate. It has real operations, a profitable installed franchise and a plausible accessible market, but does not meet the framework’s verified compounder standard. The conclusion is not that smart-meter demand is fictitious or that every disclosed receivable is uncollectible. It is that capital efficiency, cash realization and current funding are insufficiently established to translate demand into a supported per-share return.

BQS and GQS are NS because CAP is missing and G2 affects material quality inputs. IAS is NS because a supported Q and R are absent. None of the three missing point scores is replaced by its bound, midpoint, cap or a score normalized across known factors. G3 Hold alone is not the reason for quality-ranking exclusion. If financial reliability and CAP were resolved while funding remained uncertain, the company could re-enter the quality comparison without automatically becoming investable.

At the reference price, the conditional rescue Base present value of ₹126.01 is below ₹136.05, but that is not a standalone buy price or a reliable intrinsic-value estimate. It rests on favorable working-capital improvement, a 13% operating margin, an assumed equity raise and a 10 x exit EBITDA multiple. A lower market price improves mathematical returns but does not establish that the model’s financing can happen. The appropriate next action is evidence gathering and monitoring, not a price-triggered purchase based only on the historical 14.25 x P/E.

For portfolio use, no holding recommendation or position size is supplied without the user’s circumstances, mandate and risk capacity. Even a nominal ₹5 lakh reference position is not continuously divisible: three lots cost ₹4.0815 lakh and four ₹5.4420 lakh. Limit-price discipline and a realistic exit horizon would be necessary for any later authorized investment decision; this research does not execute or recommend a trade. Daily volume is an observation, not available guaranteed liquidity.

A more favorable classification requires three linked demonstrations: reconciled accounts and bank returns; funded working capital and completion commitments; and sustained cash returns from the new capital rather than just higher sales. A more adverse classification follows if old receivables fail to collect, supplier disputes obstruct operations, project capital is impaired, or financing imposes substantially worse dilution than the rescue assumptions. Management’s strategic direction and a new large shareholder are context, not replacements for those tests. The report remains open to contrary evidence and specifies what would change it.

sections.title: Sources, Assumptions & Open Questions
sections.text:
The evidence hierarchy prioritizes exchange-hosted audited reports, prospectus financials, shareholding XBRL, statutory acquisition/sale disclosures, official market archives and surveillance files. Issuer presentations and transcripts supply management claims, not audited forecasts. Historical peer reports are used for operating comparisons only, and no unsupported latest peer valuation is presented. Public secondary pages were discovery aids and are not material claim sources. Every cited item has a local retained file, source URL, document timing or an explicit unknown date, page/context locator and SHA-256 hash. Source IDs resolve to the ledger, and evidence IDs connect the 13 factor audits to their claims.

The retained archive is point-in-time disciplined. Cutoff 20 October 2026 excludes later announcements or results even though retrieval occurred 21 October. FY26 is the latest verified full financial year and is not labelled an invented September 2026 TTM. The six-year statutory history and prospectus restatements are both preserved because they are not interchangeable. FY21 tax presentation, FY23 restated profit differences, the FY25 reconciliation typo and current bank-return gaps remain visible. Source limitations reduce confidence rather than being repaired without disclosure.

The model uses a 26% normalized tax rate,12% diagnostic debt interest,1.5% depreciation/revenue, stated growth/margin/working-capital/capex paths, a ₹1 crore liquidity buffer,8/10/12 x terminal EBITDA multiples, and a 15% nominal pretax equity hurdle. The rescue issue price ₹108.84 and 5% fees are assumptions, not negotiated terms. There are no assumed dividends. Current debt repayment and equal long-term amortization are stress conventions because a complete contractual schedule and renewals are unavailable. Equity value is enterprise value less ending debt plus positive available cash; no claim is deducted twice. Negative ordinary cash invalidates returns rather than becoming negative cash added to equity value.

The unresolved questions are specific: What were September cash, draw and eligible bank limits? Which receivables were collected after March, and which are retained or disputed? Why do bank submissions differ from the books and face statements? How much capital advance moved into land or other assets, and how should its cash-flow classification be reconciled? What is the cost, ownership and useful life of the unfinished know-how? What remains to commission and fund the plant? What are the backlog schedule and cancellation rights? What commercial commitments, if any, accompany Waaree’s secondary stake? None is answered by assuming that reported equity or backlog is cash.

Reproduction requires Python standard library only: independently extract the 60 issuer rows from retained NSE archives, run the model, build the canonical dossier and run QA. The current source-free archives retain the report, evidence ledger, extracted market rows, scripts, model outputs and manifests, but exclude original issuer documents. They reproduce calculations, not a fresh audit of omitted primary sources; source re-verification requires retrieving originals from the retained URLs and checking their hashes.  No trade or third-party outreach is performed by this package.

model_limits: March 2026 balance sheet is stale at October entry. Interim balances, sanctions, borrowing base and renewals are not verified.
Years 1-5 are annual entry-date intervals ending October 2031 using FY26 baseline, not overlapping fiscal forecasts or a fabricated H1FY27.
Ordinary case repays all current debt in year one and LT debt evenly over five years as stress convention, not a claimed contractual amortization schedule.
Tax and statutory opening claims are paid once. Trade and operating provisions are included only in ONWC. BGs and FX payables are not added again to ordinary debt.
Restricted long-term deposits and loan-security deposits are not assumed freely distributable. No double counting IPO proceeds, canceled warrants or promoter secondary sale.
Capex includes the 1.4229 commitment once within year one, not as an extra claim. The 2.68 earmark releases once against capex. Expense escrow excluded from available cash is not deducted again.
Rescue shares are issued at 80% of entry price, 5% issue fees, and preserve a 1 crore cash buffer; no evidence this capital will be provided.
DA 1.5% of sales, capex and working-capital targets are analyst assumptions. P/E cross-check uses scenario equity and earnings, not a second enterprise-to-equity debt deduction.
